a:
[b]Molfar System[/b] is your personal AI council. Instead of asking one neural network, you assemble a [b]meeting[/b]: up to four AI participants from different providers (Google, NVIDIA, OpenRouter), each with its own role, answering independently.

The [b]Orchestrator[/b] is the fifth: it runs rounds, compares answers and prepares a single summary. The [b]Secretary[/b] is the sixth: it handles project documents and writes a protocol on demand.

For quick questions there is [b]Haiduk[/b] — a single chat that can be "dressed" into any role.

Your API keys stay on your device only. Project website: [ref=https://molfar.nova-hata.com][color=4db6ac][u]molfar.nova-hata.com[/u][/color][/ref]

1. Menu > [b]AI Settings[/b] > paste an API key for at least one provider (free; see "How to add an API key?").
2. Create a meeting project and fill the slots in [b]Participants settings[/b]: Orchestrator + 1–2 participants is already a working meeting.
3. Ask your question in the "Ask the Orchestrator" field — the round goes to everyone, answers gather in tabs.

For a warm-up try Haiduk: one model, zero setup.

The app is [b]free[/b]. It needs provider API keys — [b]also free[/b]: Google AI Studio, NVIDIA NIM and OpenRouter issue them on their websites.

Free models have provider-side request limits — enough for normal work. Models marked [b]$[/b] on OpenRouter are paid: they consume tokens from your OpenRouter balance. Don't want to pay — simply don't pick them.

q: How do I create a meeting?
a:
1. On the home screen create a "Meeting" project and name it.
2. [b]Participants settings[/b]: slots 1–4 — participants (role + model each), 5 — Orchestrator, 6 — Secretary. Minimum: Orchestrator + one participant. Tap "Save".
3. Optionally add [b]documents[/b] to the project and hand them to participants (the badge counter at the top of a tab).
4. Ask in the "Ask the Orchestrator" field: the round is sent to everyone, each tab shows its answer, the Orchestrator summarizes.

[b]Exports and protocol[/b]
• The three-dot menu button in any tab > export the chat to a text file (Download/Molfar_s-… folder): a header with slot/role/model, every answer signed.
• The Secretary tab > protocol command: it composes a meeting protocol with the roster and chronology and saves it as a file.
Exports are also your backup: the files live outside the app.

A role is the AI's "personality": a [b]prompt[/b] (who I am) + a [b]skill[/b] (how I work). Out of the box — [b]23 roles[/b]: 17 specialists for participants (lawyers, developers, cybersecurity, a football staff, a mathematician…) and 6 leaders for the Orchestrator (Moderator, Referee, Analyst, Project Manager, Criminal Judge, Bookmaker Analyst).

Create your own in the "Roles" section: name, description, prompt, skill — it appears in the lists alongside the built-in ones. One role works both in meetings and in Haiduk.

A [b]prompt[/b] is the system instruction defining WHO the role is: profession, character, answer style. Example: "You are an experienced lawyer, you answer formally and cite law articles."

Edit it by tapping the "Prompt" block: manually or by loading a .txt/.md file via the folder icon. It is saved into the role's prompt.md, limit 5000 characters. Write it in the language you want answers in.

A [b]skill[/b] is the role's concrete rules and steps: checklists, templates, order of actions. If the prompt says "who I am", the skill says "how exactly I work".

Orchestrator nuance: its skill is stacked [b]on top[/b] of the fixed leader-seat rules (the round mechanics are built into the app) — so in an orchestrator's skill write only the leading style and evaluation criteria, without repeating the mechanics.

q: Where do I get ready-made prompts and skills?
a:
On our website [b][ref=https://molfar.nova-hata.com][color=4db6ac][u]molfar.nova-hata.com[/u][/color][/ref][/b] — a section with ready prompts and skills for various tasks.

How to apply: save the file (.txt or .md) to your phone > open the role > the prompt or skill editor > the folder icon > pick the file. The text is inserted, "Save" — and the role is ready. Your file's name doesn't matter: the editor saves it as prompt.md / skill.md.

q: Who is the Secretary and what is a protocol?
a:
The [b]Secretary[/b] is slot 6 with two jobs:
• [b]Knowledge base[/b]: it indexes all project documents and serves them to participants as fragments — so meetings work even with large files.
• [b]Protocol[/b]: on command it composes a meeting document — the roster (slot · role · model), chronology, conclusions — and saves it as a file.

Assign it a model — its working rules are built in, no role needed. The counter in its tab shows the whole project document pool.

A project has a shared [b]document pool[/b] (added in the project card or via the Secretary tab). From the pool files are handed to participants: the badge counter at the top of a tab > pick up to [b]5 files per slot[/b].

A participant sees only its own documents. Small files go into the context in full; large ones the Secretary serves as [b]fragments[/b] from the knowledge base — matched to your question.

Haiduk has its own documents: the paperclip, up to 5 files, 1 MB each.

q: What is Haiduk and how does it differ from a meeting?
Web search (globe): what does it do and why is it sometimes unavailable?
a:
The [b]globe[/b] enables web search: the model gets fresh results from the internet and cites sources (title + address).

It doesn't work everywhere: not all providers and models support search — then the globe is inactive. On OpenRouter web search is [b]paid[/b] — the app warns before enabling. With search off, the model answers from its own knowledge and never claims it "searched the web".

q: How to add an API key?
a:
Menu > [b]AI Settings[/b] > paste the key into the provider's field > tap the diskette icon. The provider turns on automatically.

Where to get free keys:
• [b]Google[/b]: [ref=https://aistudio.google.com/apikey][color=4db6ac][u]aistudio.google.com/apikey[/u][/color][/ref] > "Create API key"
• [b]NVIDIA[/b]: [ref=https://build.nvidia.com][color=4db6ac][u]build.nvidia.com[/u][/color][/ref] > sign up > "Get API Key" on any model page
• [b]OpenRouter[/b]: [ref=https://openrouter.ai/keys][color=4db6ac][u]openrouter.ai/keys[/u][/color][/ref] > "Create Key"

The "Test" button checks the connection. Keys are stored on this device only.

q: Where are my data and keys stored?
a:
Everything is local, on your device: projects, histories, roles, documents and API keys live in the app folder. Nothing is sent to Molfar servers; keys go only to the AI providers themselves at request time.

The flip side: [b]uninstalling the app deletes all data[/b]. What survives: chat exports and protocols — they are saved in Download/Molfar… and live separately. Export the meetings that matter.

q: The model doesn't answer or shows an error — what to do?
a:
Check in order:
1. [b]Key[/b]: AI Settings > the provider's "Test" button.
2. [b]Limits[/b]: free models have request limits — wait a minute or switch the model.
3. [b]Timeout[/b] ("did not respond in 220 s"): a heavy question + large documents — simplify the request or pick a faster model.
4. An error with the provider's text — the problem is on their side: try another model or later.

If the app crashed — the screen shows a report with a copy button: send it to us via the website.

q: How do I delete a project and what disappears?
a:
The project card menu > "Delete". [b]Everything of it[/b] disappears: chats of all slots, the roster, documents (files and assignments), the knowledge base, long-term memory.

What stays: exports and protocols in Download (they are outside the app) and the roles themselves — they are shared across projects.

The action is irreversible — export the important things first.
